title: continuous-batching-scheduler-tuning-experiments-notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This notes doc captures a set of controlled experiments we ran to tune the continuous-batching scheduler. Goal was to reduce p95/p99 tail latency without sacrificing >10% throughput across common production traces (chatty short-turn vs long-turn generations). We focused on four knobs: max_batch_size, emit_timeout_ms, fairness mode, and emitter backpressure behavior.

Testbed and workload:
- Model: redwood-compat-13B-ml (fp16 kernel selection) on a single a100.
- Serving runtime build: master@2026-01-18 + scheduler-experiments branch.
- Workload traces: (A) chatty: 75% requests 8 tokens, 25% 64 tokens, poisson inter-arrival with mean lambda=40 req/s. (B) batched-doc: 30% 256 tokens, 70% 128 tokens, lambda=12 req/s.
- Concurrency: 32 worker threads, async IO loop enabled.
- KV cache warm vs cold: majority tests run with warmed KV. Cold-start spot-checks separately.
- Measurement: measured p50/p95/p99 tail in ms (wall), tokens/sec, and batching efficiency (average batch fill fraction). Each run = 20 minutes steady state, warmup 3 minutes.

Baseline scheduler behavior:
- Default: max_batch_size=64, emit_timeout_ms=20, fairness=fifo. Observed baseline metrics (trace A): p50=72ms, p95=182ms, p99=420ms, throughput=48k tokens/s, avg_batch_fill=0.42.

Experiment matrix (summarized):
- Varied max_batch_size in {16,32,64,128}
- Varied emit_timeout_ms in {5,10,20,50}
- Fairness modes: fifo | weighted_latency_first (weights by queue wait time) | priority_small_first (prefer small requests to reduce tail)

Key findings (short):
1) Small batches + short timeout reduced p95 significantly for chatty traces but reduced throughput for long-turn workloads. Example: max_batch_size=16 + timeout=5ms + priority_small_first => trace A p95 ~120ms (vs baseline 182ms), p99 ~300ms, throughput -18%.
2) Weighted_latency_first balanced tail vs throughput best across mixed workloads. With max_batch_size=64 + timeout=10ms latency-first weights=0.6 -> p95 140ms, throughput -6%, avg_fill 0.62.
3) Larger max_batch_size (128) improved tokens/sec (up to +12%) on batched-doc but made chatty p99 explode (700ms+) unless timeout reduced aggressively.
4) Emit timeout has nonlinear effects: going from 20ms->10ms reduces p95 by ~15-25% for chatty inputs and only ~5% throughput loss when paired with dynamic fairness. 5ms aggressive low-latency setting gives best p95 but harms batch efficiency and increases GPU kernel overhead (more kernel launches).
5) Cold KV scenarios increase p99 by ~30% across configs; batching knobs don't mitigate this — we need different kernel warm paths / prefetching.

Representative configs to consider for product rollout:
- Balanced mode (recommended for hosted default): max_batch_size=64, emit_timeout_ms=10, fairness=weighted_latency_first (weight_alpha=0.6), backpressure_limit=1024 inflight tokens. Rationale: best mix of p95 reduction (~20%) and throughput loss (~5-8%).
- Low-latency chat mode (opt-in): max_batch_size=32, emit_timeout_ms=5, fairness=priority_small_first. Use for interactive apps where tail matters more than unit cost.
- Throughput mode (dedicated capacity): max_batch_size=128, emit_timeout_ms=50, fairness=fifo. For bulk embedding/long generation workloads.

Profiling notes / bottlenecks observed:
- Kernel launch overhead becomes visible at batch sizes <32 with high arrival rate; nontrivial fraction of time in cuBLAS setup and memcpy. Consider consolidating small kernels or reusing streams.
- Scheduler locking: hotspots in queue scanning when many priorities present (we saw lock contention spikes in flame graphs around scheduler::pop()). Sketch: convert to sharded queues by hash of request size bucket to reduce contention.
- Unbalanced batch composition: heterogeneous token-length mixing increases per-token latency variance; adding length-aware grouping (cohorting) reduced p99 by ~12% but slightly reduced avg_fill.

Detailed run snapshots (selected):
- Run R-2026-01-22-A (trace A, max_batch_size=32, timeout=10, fairness=weighted_latency_first): p50=64ms, p95=128ms, p99=280ms, tokens/s=39.6k, avg_fill=0.58. GPU util 78%.
- Run R-2026-01-24-B (trace B, max_batch_size=128, timeout=50, fairness=fifo): p50=110ms, p95=210ms, p99=620ms, tokens/s=68.3k, avg_fill=0.86.

Commands / artifacts to reproduce:
- run script: ./bench/run_continuous_batch.sh --model redwood-compat-13B-ml --trace chatty.json --duration 1200 --max-batch 64 --timeout-ms 10 --fairness weighted_latency_first
- profiler flags: SERVE_PROFILE=1 SERVE_PROFILE_OUT=run-A-32-10.prof; use pyflame / perf to collect CPU+mutex; nvprof / Nsight for GPU slices.

Open questions and next steps:
- Can we implement a hybrid emitter that dynamically reduces timeout during high QPS short-turn phases and increases timeout for long-turn bursts? (Adaptive timeout)
- Feasibility of sharded scheduling queues to reduce lock contention — prototype in scheduler-experiments branch.
- Investigate kernel fusion / pooled stream strategy to reduce per-infer kernel overhead for small batches.
- Add continuous rolling experiments in staging to validate impact on cost per 1M tokens and error rates for production traffic patterns.
- Longer-term: autoscaling signals that consider batch_fill and emitted latency to avoid oscillation between latency and throughput modes.

Action items (owners):
- (Asha) Push adaptive-timeout prototype + unit tests (target: 2026-02-28).
- (Diego) Prototype sharded-queue variant and microbench profile (target: 2026-03-10).
- (Lina) Run 72h soak with balanced config on dedicated pool to gather cost curve and p99 tail (target: 2026-03-05).
- (Marcus) Investigate kernel pooling patterns and prepare perf notes (target: 2026-02-28).

Notes to reviewer:
- These experiments are synthetic; before shipping defaults, we need to run on sampled production traces and confirm fairness settings don't regresses specific customers.
- I intentionally left per-request SLAs as a follow-up; most customers buy Dedicated for throughput guarantees and Private for control over kernel stack.

Misc scratch / ideas:
- Consider a small-request fast-path that bypasses the main scheduling queue (single-producer lock-free ring) to reduce serialization for sub-16-token requests.
- Explore combining prefix caching heuristics with scheduler priority (requests hitting cached KV get lower priority).

End of notes.
